hints.title: Contiguous Window Formulation
hints.text: For any contiguous subarray of k robots from index left to right, the total cost is max(chargeTimes[left..right]) + k * sum(runningCosts[left..right]).

hints.title: Sliding Range Expansion
hints.text: Use a sliding two-pointer window [left, right] while tracking the running cost sum and the maximum charge time.

hints.title: Monotonic Deque Maximum
hints.text: Maintain a monotonic decreasing double-ended queue storing indices of chargeTimes to extract the window maximum in O(1) amortized time.

hints.title: Sliding Window Budget Deque Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from collections import deque

class Solution:
    def maximumRobots(self, chargeTimes: list[int], runningCosts: list[int], budget: int) -> int:
        q = deque()
        left = 0
        cur_sum = 0
        max_len = 0
        
        for right in range(len(chargeTimes)):
            cur_sum += runningCosts[right]
            while q and chargeTimes[q[-1]] <= chargeTimes[right]:
                q.pop()
            q.append(right)
            
            while left <= right and chargeTimes[q[0]] + (right - left + 1) * cur_sum > budget:
                if q[0] == left:
                    q.popleft()
                cur_sum -= runningCosts[left]
                left += 1
            
            max_len = max(max_len, right - left + 1)
        return max_len
```

complexity.notes: Each index is pushed and popped at most once in the monotonic deque.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating every subarray maximum charge time naively takes O(n^2) or O(n^3) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Monotonic deque stores decreasing candidates for constant-time window maximum queries.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Combines sliding window accumulator with monotonic deque for optimal linear execution.
